subject: CustKey data-flow gates & subprocessor gating for private deployment

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: CustKey data-flow gates & subprocessor gating for private deployment

Carlos / Medisys team —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As promised, I’m sending a concise proposal for how we can operationalize two things you raised: (1) customer-controlled keys (BYOK) with strict operator gating, and (2) a subprocessor gating process tied to deployment-specific egress controls. Attached: Proposed_Gating_Checklist.xlsx and BYOK_Operator_Sequence.pdf.

High-level ask from us to you so we can draft the DPA addendum:
- Confirm whether the HSM will be a customer-managed HSM in your VPC (yes/no).
- Provide target list of allowed external integrations (sending destinations) that must be whitelisted in egress policies.
- Clarify whether Medisys requires escrow exceptions or if the expectation is no escrow at all.

Proposed constraints from Redwood (draft):
- Operators: Redwood operators will have zero direct access to decryption keys. Breakglass access allowed only via an audited, time-limited, two-person approval flow (canary + 4-eyes) with full session recording and immutable audit logs exported to your logging infrastructure.
- Subprocessor gating: Any subprocessor that needs network egress from your isolated deployment must be pre-approved via a gating ticket; approval will consider geofencing, SOC2/ISO evidence, and a minimum SLA.
- Egress: All egress must terminate through a customer-managed gateway or proxy controlled by your network team; we will only permit TLS to those endpoints and enforce IP/TLS certificate pinning as requested.

Next steps I propose: Redwood to provide a short DPA addendum draft reflecting those controls; Legal to provide redlines; Security teams to align on evidence pack and list of allowed subprocessors.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few points from Medisys Legal & Security:
1) BYOK escrows: default position is no third-party escrow. We will consider a vendor-managed escrow only under a strict MSA appendix with notarized access and jurisdictional constraints.
2) Subprocessor gating: we require a 10-business-day notice for any new subprocessor plus a written attestation that the subprocessor’s data access is limited to telemetry (no cleartext model inputs/outputs).
3) Operator breakglass: acceptable if access is ephemeral, fully auditable, and requires Medisys SRE sign-off for each event.

I’ve attached initial redlines to your suggested DPA language. Please review and incorporate where feasible.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Senior Counsel, Medisys Health

Looping internal ops/procurement notes into the thread:

Operational notes / suggested changes for negotiation:
- Egress enforcement: prefer the model where all outbound connections from the private deployment use a customer side proxy (we’ll support mutual TLS to that proxy and validate client certs). This satisfies most egress concerns and keeps us from needing to manage network-level firewall rules for each subprocessor.
- Evidence pack: Security will provide SOC2 type II snapshots and subprocessors’ security packs on a per-request basis. We should avoid including full lists of subprocessors in the DPA — instead reference the gating process and provide an annex for specific integrations.
- Procurement: if Medisys requires a 10-business-day notice window for new subprocessors, procurement will add standard language for timeline SLAs and acceptance criteria to the SOW addendum.

Irene — please confirm whether the operator breakglass flow Jonas described is implementable from a runtime/telemetry perspective.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

Laur en / team —

Technical confirmation and suggested implementation pattern below. Attached: BYOK_Operator_SeqDiagram.png (illustrative).

Technical proposal (concise):
- Key custody: Customer-managed CMK in their HSM; Redwood will hold an administrative reference only (opaque handle). All cryptographic operations that need the key will be performed in-customer HSM via a short-lived mutual-TLS tunnel initiated by the HSM proxy. No plaintext keys are stored in Redwood control plane.
- Operator access gating: Implement a staged gating service: (a) Canary: automated sentinel job that requires no human interaction and proves the environment is healthy; (b) Escalation: on-call operator flow with an immutable justification ticket; (c) 4-eyes approval for any operation that requests key-material usage beyond telemetry. Every breakglass event will capture stdout/stderr, session video, command hashes, and export logs to Medisys’ S3 bucket.
- Subprocessor network gating: Use an allowlist model enforced at the instance egress layer. New subprocessors are only allowed after a gating ticket is accepted and after a minimal hygiene scan (vuln scan + cert check). We can export automated attestations back to your governance tracker.
- Dataflow restrictions: At the application layer, redact or tokenise PII before any telemetry leaves the environment unless explicitly permitted. We’ll add a telemetry schema and a sample redaction pipeline to the evidence pack.

I’m comfortable implementing the above with the caveat that we’ll need to agree on monitoring retention windows and log export endpoints.

Irene Choi
Director, Security Engineering — Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good progress and we have enough to move forward with a concrete next step list. Agreed items and immediate action items: 

Agreed:
- Medisys will not accept broad vendor escrow without a separate notarized appendix; default is no escrow.
- Operator breakglass allowed with 4-eyes and Medisys SRE sign-off; all session artifacts exported to your logging bucket.
- New subprocessors require gating ticket + hygiene evidence + 10-business-day notice.

Action items:
- Redwood Legal: produce DPA addendum draft incorporating the gating language and egress model (target: EOD Fri).
- Medisys Legal: provide redline feedback on the attached redlines.
- Medisys Security: provide initial list of high-priority allowed endpoints (ip/hostnames) for egress enforcement within 3 business days.
- Redwood Security (Irene): prepare evidence pack (SOC2 snapshot, minimal hygiene checklist, sample telemetry redaction rules).
- Procurement: Jonas will share Requested_Subprocessors_List_template.csv for Medisys to populate.

I’ll open a shared JIRA and a gating ticket template after Redwood Legal pushes the addendum. Thanks all — if there are no objections I’ll move to create the JIRA/DocuSign packet today.

Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
